title: Francesco Babbi's cipher avvisi from Ferrara, 1551-1555: three full pages of figures, bare; a decipherment of his system exists
correspondents: Francesco Babbi, Florentine agent at Ferrara -> Cosimo I
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo del Principato 402 A, c. 675; 444, c. 127; 445, c. 386
folio_note: 402 A c. 675r (s.d., filed 9 May 1551, to ***): a full page of figures (vol. IV p. 271); 444 c. 127r ("Avviso in cifra di [Francesco Babbi]", [1555], filed with Babbi's letters of 18-19 Mar 1555): a full page; 445 c. 386r (same title, filed inside Babbi's letter of 14 Apr 1555, cc. 385, 387): a full page. Inventory vol. VII pp. 389, 412 and index: "Babbi Francesco, avviso in cifra, 1555: 444, 127; 445, 368; 386".
status: Bare: no gloss on the three pages; neighbours are clear (402 A c. 674, c. 676 Ferrari; 444 cc. 126, 128 avvisi; 445 cc. 385, 387 Babbi's covering letter). Key material: 445 c. 368 (Babbi avviso) with its decipherment at c. 367 (inventory note 52, "Questa cifra è usata ufficialmente da Francesco Babbi ... La decifrazione è a c. 367"), 444 c. 113 (Babbi, 18 Mar 1555, interlinear decipherment, note 9), and the key in ASF Cifrari II serie F. III.
why: A series in one keyed system from the Este court during the war of Siena; the glossed siblings let the key be rebuilt and the bare avvisi read.
verify: Rebuild the key from 445 cc. 367-368 and 444 c. 113; apply to the three bare pages; check 402 A c. 845 (Babbi insert sent via "il Sarto", not found on the PAD carte 845-846).

title: Bernardo Rucellai, Florentine orator in Milan, July-September 1482: four bare letters in his sign cipher, with three glossed siblings in the same filza
correspondents: Bernardo Rucellai, orator in Milan -> Lorenzo de' Medici
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXII, docs. 196, 200, 202, 206
folio_note: Each a single leaf, recto, opening in clear and running into long sign-cipher passages between clear words: 196 (old c. 238; inventory "(Milano, 1482 lug. 3)", about 20 lines), 200 (c. 243; "lug. 19", about 15 lines), 202 (c. 245; "lug. 11", about 15 lines), 206 (c. 249; "set. 4", about 8 lines with dotted gaps). MAP inventory vol. 3, filza LXXII: "(Bernardo Rucellai). (Milano, 1482 lug. 3), n. 196; (lug. 15), n. 201; lug. 19, n. 200; (lug. 11), n. 202; (ago. 30), n. 204; n. 205; (set. 4), n. 206; (giu. 3), n. 211"; none flagged as cipher.
status: Bare: no interlinear or marginal decipherment on 196, 200, 202 or 206 (900 px, crops). Key material in the same run: 201 (15 Jul) carries interlinear glosses over many cipher groups; 205 is the clear text of 204 (30 Aug; it opens with the same words, "Noi diremo che noi contraffacciamo ..."); 208 is the decipherment of 207 (inventory "Decifrato della n. 207"). Lead 2323 (LXXII 211) is the 3 June 1482 letter of this series (inventory attribution to Rucellai).
why: A run of cipher despatches from Milan in the War of Ferrara (1482), with three glossed letters of the same system beside them: a key can be rebuilt and the four bare letters (and lead 2323) read.
verify: Rebuild the sign table from 204/205, 207/208 and the glosses on 201; apply to 196, 200, 202, 206 and lead 2323 (211); compare with the 1483 Rucellai cipher of XLVIII 214 (catalogue), said to use a different sign set.

title: Roberto Acciaiuoli, Florentine orator in France, Amiens 23 October 1513: two sides of homophonic cipher, bare; a glossed letter of the same day gives the key
correspondents: Roberto Acciaiuoli, orator at the French court -> [Giuliano de' Medici / the Medici in Florence]
language: Italian (sign cipher with superscript homophone marks)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXII, doc. 192 (old c. 234)
folio_note: One leaf: recto opens "Mag.ce Vir" then about 15 lines of letter-signs, many with small superscript digits (3, 4, 5); the verso about 14 more lines of the same. MAP inventory vol. 3: "Robertus Acciarolus, orator. Ex Amiens, 1513 ott. 23, n. 192" (no cipher flag).
status: Bare (900 px, recto and verso). Key material: doc. 190 (c. 232), Acciaiuoli's cipher letter of the same day in the same system (signed "Robertus Acciarolus", "Ex Amiens die xxiii Octobris MDXIII"), and doc. 191 (c. 233), "Copia di lettera di Ruberto Acciaioli da Amiens ...", which repeats the text of 190 in clear ("Oltre alle lettere publiche ... Sanseverino ... arrivò adì xx la sera"): a full plaintext for 190.
why: The Florentine ambassador at Louis XII's court in the year after the Medici restoration; the key can be rebuilt from 190/191 and 192 read.
verify: Align 190 with 191 to rebuild the homophonic table (superscripts included); apply to 192 r-v.

title: Piero Dovizi da Bibbiena, Venice, 8 September 1512: two sides of clear text with many sign-cipher runs, bare
correspondents: Piero Dovizi da Bibbiena (Venice) -> [the Medici: Cardinal Giovanni or Giuliano de' Medici]
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXII, doc. 189 (old cc. 230-231)
folio_note: cc. 230r-231r: a long letter in clear with frequent cipher runs in single letter-like signs (several runs a line, some underlined), naming Bernardo Rucellai and ser Giovanni di ser Bartolomeo in clear. MAP inventory vol. 3: "Petrus (Dovizi da) Bibiena. Venetiis, 1512 set. 8, n. 189". A separate strip, doc. 189 bis, is a partial cipher alphabet (keys.json).
status: Bare (900 px; crops of both sides): no interlinear gloss; 190-191 are Acciaiuoli's 1513 pair, not a decipherment of this letter. The 189 bis alphabet strip was not matched against these signs.
why: A Medici agent in Venice writing in cipher a week after the Medici returned to Florence (Sept 1512); many short runs between clear words make it a good crib target.
verify: Transcribe; compare the sign set with the 189 bis strip and the LXXII key sheets 178-188; solve from the clear context.

folio_note: One leaf, recto: about 28 lines of continuous letter-like signs (Latin letters, crosses, Greek-like forms), no clear word, no address; verso blank. MAP inventory vol. 4 lists CXIX 115-127 together as "Cifre della segreteria di Lorenzo il Magnifico col duca di Urbino, col duca di Calabria, con Giovanni Tornabuoni, con l'ambasciatore di Venezia, Paolo Antonio Soderini, con Lodovico Sforza, con Piero Medici, con Costanzo Sforza, con Dionigi Mortellas, con Giovan Battista Centurioni, con Pellegrino (Rossi) da Forlì, con Ranuccio (Farnese)": twelve keys named for thirteen documents; 126 is the one that is a text, not a table.
status: Bare (900 px). The twelve key sheets beside it (CXIX 115-125, 127; keys.json) are the obvious first test.
why: An unread Laurentian cipher text filed with twelve keys of the same chancery: very likely readable with one of them.
verify: Build the sign inventory of 126; match it against the alphabets of CXIX 115-125, 127 and LXXII 178-188.
